Definition: from G2839; a sharer, i.e. associate:--companion, X fellowship, partaker, partner.
KeyPassages: Matthew 23:30; Luke 5:10; 1 Corinthians 10:18; 2 Corinthians 1:7; Philemon 1:17; Hebrews 10:33
BiblicalUsage: Koinonos is a sharer, a companion, a partner. Matthew 23:30 has the Pharisees claiming they would not have been partakers with their fathers in the blood of the prophets, Luke 5:10 names James and John as partners with Simon, 1 Corinthians 10:18 asks, are not they which eat of the sacrifices partakers of the altar, 2 Corinthians 1:7 says, as ye are partakers of the sufferings, so shall ye be also of the consolation, Philemon 1:17 has Paul asking Philemon to receive Onesimus as a partner, and Hebrews 10:33 remembers those who became companions of them that were afflicted.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a partner is known by what he shares: the altar, the suffering, the consolation, and the afflicted. I hold that Paul's ask in Philemon 1:17 is the boldest use of the word, because he asks Philemon to receive a runaway slave as he would receive Paul himself.
